profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, NY2, mapped here as the Secaucus Campus, is located at 2 Emerson Lane, Secaucus, NJ 07094. CoreSite's figures disagree across its own materials: the live facility page states more than 256,000 square feet, while the operator's own spec-sheet landing page instead gives more than 236,000 square feet; both come from CoreSite itself, and this entry flags the discrepancy rather than picking one. No MW capacity or opening year is stated. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally. CoreSite's New York-market footprint also includes NY1 in Manhattan (32 Avenue of the Americas) and NY3, a separate facility this registry tracks that shares NY2's published street address on CoreSite's own site.

CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a total portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500-plus connected network providers.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across the Secaucus/New York cluster among CoreSite's other markets.

profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite facility is in one of the company confirmed operating markets. Wikipedia coverage states that as of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with key locations including Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, Northern Virginia, San Francisco/San Jose, Santa Clara, Atlanta, Orlando, and Washington, D.C. In May 2007 the company acquired Chicago properties as part of a wider expansion. CoreSite began operating a Washington, D.C. facility in August 2005, one of its earliest East Coast sites after founding in 2001 as CRG West. CoreSite rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009, went public in September 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific market was confirmed as an active CoreSite location, but no market specific acquisition date or building history beyond the general company timeline was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite Secaucus is a 256,000 square foot facility in Hudson County, New Jersey with compliance certifications for SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA workloads. The operator does not publish power capacity for this building, making it impossible to assess its current scale relative to AI infrastructure demand. CoreSite's parent company American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite in 2026 and budgeted $695 million for data center development that year, including expansion in the Secaucus cluster, suggesting active investment in this location.

Secaucus ranks sixth among New Jersey's mapped data center facilities by published megawatt capacity, though this ranking reflects only the five New Jersey facilities with public power figures, totaling 111.3 MW across all published sites in the state. Without a published power figure for this campus, its actual position in the state's capacity is unknown. New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities overall, the vast majority of which publish no capacity data.

The facility's significance for AI scaling cannot be determined from published specifications. Power availability and cost in the Hudson County location would be the primary factors determining whether this building can host accelerator clusters, but CoreSite does not disclose either the current power delivery to Secaucus or the infrastructure headroom available for incremental load. The operator's investment signals suggest confidence in the market, but they do not substitute for disclosed capacity metrics.
